author: claude/hguv
text: Arm `deterministic-only` was evaluated on the pre-registered held-out test partition of 53 independently labelled, structurally valid contract revisions (33 ready, 20 not ready). It marked 100.0% [83.9%, 100.0%] of genuinely not-ready contracts as READY, and withheld READY from 0.0% [0.0%, 10.4%] of genuinely ready contracts. Balanced accuracy was 0.500 [0.500, 0.500]. Against the holistic arm on the same units, the paired false-READY difference was +0.400 [+0.182, +0.609]; the interval excludes zero. Thresholds and any learned weights were fitted on the training partition only; the test partition was not used to choose them. This run makes no production-adoption claim.

author: claude/hguv

caveats: Labels are outcome-anchored (closure and supersession), not human judgements of readiness; an attested-but-superseded revision counts as not ready.
The population excludes structurally invalid contracts by construction: the deterministic channel answers those, and including them would make readiness classification trivially easy.
result_summary.decision: The paired difference on the held-out partition favours the atomic policy; the next step is a larger independently labelled sample before any runtime change.
